elements.element: Fallback: licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice
elements.evidence: "grants to Customer and, on written notice to Kubient, its affiliates a limited, royalty-free ... license"

elements.element: Fallback: licence transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "non-assignable except to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets"

elements.element: Preferred: licence extends to Customer's affiliates (without notice condition)
elements.evidence: affiliate coverage is conditioned: "on written notice to Kubient, its affiliates"

elements.element: Preferred: licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: grant runs only to "Customer and, on written notice to Kubient, its affiliates"; no contractor language, and "without right of sublicense" remains

elements.element: Preferred: paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: licence remains "revocable license to access, participate in and use"

elements.element: Preferred: subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: no termination standard added; grant stays "revocable"
"except to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets"

reasons: Both fallback atomic elements are satisfied by a single targeted edit: affiliates are brought within the grant on written notice, and the non-assignability restriction is carved back for an M&A successor.

Preferred level is not reached — the licence is still expressly "revocable", there is no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up right, no uncured-material-breach-only termination standard, and no contractor coverage (sublicensing remains barred). This is consistent with the locked fallback target and adds no preferred-only scope or duration.
Minimality holds: two short in-line insertions into the existing grant sentence; no rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate.

Intent preserved: royalty-free, non-exclusive, no-sublicense, purpose limitation and the Google Ad Manager mechanic are untouched; "affiliates" and "successor" are used in their ordinary sense without creating dangling defined terms.
